subject: MSA + Order Form: allocation of defense control vs. reimbursement for model-output claims
messages:
From: Sara Burns <sara.burns@northbridge.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@northbridge.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: MSA + Order Form: indemnity approach for model-output allegations

Hi Logan / Kim,

Thanks for sending the draft MSA and order form redlines. Attached are Northbridge's initial redlines (NB_redlines_MSA.docx and OrderForm_redline.pdf). Two items that need immediate alignment from a commercial/legal perspective:

1) Defense control for third-party IP claims: Northbridge expects Redwood to defend and control any third-party IP claims arising out of the Services (patents, copyrights) and to indemnify for amounts finally awarded.

2) Claims tied to AI-generated output: Northbridge is asking for a broader indemnity for any claim by a third party alleging that AI output delivered by the Service infringes IP or otherwise causes liability. At minimum we need clarity whether Redwood will 'defend and control' these claims or merely reimburse.

Operational asks:
- Notice timing: we propose 30 days after the customer receives notice.
- Evidence preservation and access: counsel will need access to logs/outputs and a contact for evidence staging.
- Insurance: please confirm the applicable professional liability/AI coverage and limits.

Can you confirm Redwood's position on defend vs reimburse for model-output claims? Also please let us know if you want to propose alternate language; we prefer to resolve scope prior to the procurement committee meeting next Wednesday.

Regards,
Sara Burns
Counsel, Northbridge Health
Sara.Burns@northbridge.com

Attachments: NB_redlines_MSA.docx (tracked), OrderForm_redline.pdf

From: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>
To: Sara Burns <sara.burns@northbridge.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: indemnity approach for model-output allegations

Sara, thanks — received. Looping in Kim (contracts) and Naomi (legal) to confirm our position and proposed language.

High-level summary of Redwood's commercial view:
- For "classic" third-party IP claims (patent/copyright related to the Services), Redwood is prepared to defend and control and indemnify subject to the usual MSA limits and carveouts.
- For claims that arise from AI-generated output (claims that a model response/answer infringes or causes loss), our preferred position is reimbursement-only with a reasonable cap and collaborative evidence process. The reasoning is that outputs are co-produced with Customer prompts and often dependent on customer data and use.

Operational items we need to resolve now:
- Proposed cap for output-related reimbursements (we typically start at $250k–$500k per claim).
- Evidence custody: what logs/outputs do Northbridge need and will there be an agreed evidence-preservation window?
- Notice timing and cure: 30 days notice for claims is standard for both sides.

Kim / Naomi — can you weigh in on an acceptable cap and draft redline we should send back? Northbridge needs an answer before next Wed procurement review.

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
logan@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0173

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: Sara Burns <sara.burns@northbridge.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan@redwood.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@northbridge.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: indemnity approach for model-output allegations

Sara, appreciate the clarity. I've reviewed Northbridge's redlines and sketched a compromise clause to move the deal forward. Key points below and attached is a tracked clause (RFQ_OrderForm_Clause_v3.docx).

Proposed compromise (high level):
- Redwood will defend and control third-party intellectual property infringement claims that (i) relate to the Services as delivered by Redwood (including underlying model code and hosted service) and (ii) do not arise solely from Customer-provided content or Customer modifications. Redwood will indemnify for amounts finally awarded and reasonable settlement amounts.
- For claims specifically alleging that AI-generated output (the "Output") infringes a third party's IP or causes loss, Redwood will not accept unilateral defense control. Instead, Redwood will reimburse Customer's reasonable costs and settlement amounts up to a per-claim cap of $500,000, provided Customer: (a) gives notice to Redwood within 30 days of receipt of the claim; (b) preserves relevant artifacts and output; and (c) reasonably cooperates with Redwood's investigation.
- Redwood requests a reciprocal obligation for Customer to notify and cooperate on claims to the extent Customer has control or knowledge; subrogation rights will apply if Redwood reimburses and later recovers.
- For clarity, open-source training-data assertions and warranty claims tied to Customer-introduced content will be excluded from Redwood's defense obligations.

Operational asks for Northbridge: please confirm preferred contact for evidence staging and whether your security team requires a data-retention SLA for outputs. If the $500k cap is a blocker, provide a target number and we will escalate.

On the notice/timing: 30 days is reasonable. We can add a short cure/mitigation window in the clause.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com

Subject: Re: MSA + Order Form: indemnity approach for model-output allegations — legal signoff path

Sara, Kim — thanks for the back-and-forth. I reviewed Kim's proposed compromise and can sign off on the approach with two clarifications we should add to the redline:

1) Subrogation and recovery mechanics: If Redwood reimburses Customer under the output-reimbursement path and later recovers from a third party, Redwood may deduct recoveries from amounts reimbursed. We should add explicit assignment/subrogation language and a short recovery cooperation clause.

2) Evidence preservation & privilege: Add a 6-month preservation window for relevant outputs/logs after notice, with a confidentiality carveout to allow Redwood counsel to review. Also add a narrow privilege-protection procedure to avoid waiver.

3) Mutuality & step-in rights: For third-party IP claims Redwood agrees to defend and control, we should add a mutuality comfort: Redwood has primary control but Customer may participate with counsel at Customer's cost unless Customer's participation creates a conflict, in which case Redwood will step in.

4) Insurance confirmation: Please provide Northbridge's expected PL/Tech E&O limits. We will confirm Redwood's policy and available limits to populate the order form insurance fields.

If Northbridge accepts those clarifications, we can circulate a clean redline for signature. Adding this to HubSpot (deal HUBSPOT-123456) and marking for procurement review.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Deputy General Counsel | Redwood Inference
naomi@redwood.com

Thanks Naomi / Kim — this framework is helpful and Northbridge is prepared to accept the two-path approach: (1) full defense/control + indemnity for service-level third-party IP; and (2) reimbursement with a per-claim cap for AI-output allegations, subject to the subrogation and preservation mechanics you outlined.

Please send the revised tracked clause (including the 6-month preservation window, subrogation assignment language, and the mutuality step-in language). Once we have Redwood's final clause (we will review internally with procurement), I can confirm insurance numbers and we can move to signature.
